skills.summary: Use decimal notation in numerical work.
Work with standard form.
Use ratios, fractions, percentages, powers and roots.
Choose suitable significant figures.

taskMappings.rationale: Select recalled substance properties from a fixed list. The task does not ask for a practical method, measurement or separate listed mathematical operation.
Describe a suitable gas-identification procedure with the associated observation; no practical is performed.
Interpret the supplied water/acid observations to infer a complete relative reactivity order.
Use the observed reaction pattern to select a metal identity consistent with the data.
Apply chemical knowledge to the specified metal/acid reaction within the experimental table context.
Use the supplied no-reaction observations to choose a chemically compatible metal.
Explain the safety reason for omitting one dilute-acid test. Hazard control is not automatically an accuracy/validity evaluation under bullet10.
Define an energy-change term. A reaction context alone does not create a separate practical-demand link.
Explain displacement using chemical reactivity; no experimental evidence interpretation or numerical operation is separately demanded.
Explain oxidation/reduction for the given chemical equation. Optional number-based explanations are not treated as a compulsory mathematical operation.
Read electron-shell structure to identify a group. Counting outer electrons is chemical diagram interpretation, not a separately evidenced Appendix4 numerical demand.
Read occupied shells to identify a period. A chemical representation is not automatically a graph or a Chemistry-applicable geometry row.
Derive a compound formula from valency. This chemical formula task does not independently establish algebraic-equation assessment.
Multiply the given atom count in standard form by the electrons per atom. No source-invented precision requirement.
Use abundance percentages to form a weighted relative atomic mass. The requested one decimal place is not treated as a significant-figure demand.
Identify the element from configuration/proton identity; no listed practical or mathematical skill is separately demanded.
Count atoms in the supplied formula using integer addition. Do not equate any counting operation with a required decimal-notation skill.
Substitute supplied atom counts and atomic masses into the relative formula mass sum.
Reduce the molecular atom-count ratio to its simplest whole-number ratio.
Apply knowledge to identify the separation method from the apparatus. Naming the method is not treated as a full method-description or investigation-planning demand.
Apply the relevant state-change knowledge to the named part of the separation apparatus.
Explain bonding, structure and melting-point differences. Similar supplied relative masses do not require a new mass calculation or numerical trend plot.
Explain the placement of starting spots as a method requirement that protects a valid separation.
Interpret the chromatogram evidence to compare sample composition. Same-level comparison does not require conversion into numerical graph data.
Distinguish a supported one-dye conclusion from uncertainty when a spot has not moved; evaluate the limits of the evidence.

Measure two travel distances from the same baseline and calculate their dimensionless ratio. Physical presentation remains uncalibrated. Measure distances from the source diagram with a common reference line, solve the practical ratio problem and communicate the numerical finding. On-screen physical scale is not validated.
Describe observable changes for the teacher demonstration using suitable observation language; do not claim the learner collected measurements.
Apply indicator chemistry to interpret the resulting solution observation.
Explain a preparation step in a flame-test method and how contamination would affect the result.
Apply chemical knowledge to predict the flame colour for the named ions. No supplied unknown observation is interpreted, so bullet7 is not linked.
Supply ion formulas. The ionic-charge notation is chemical representation, not an independent mathematical symbol/equation demand.

Subtract to obtain water mass, convert masses into amounts, then determine the whole-number hydration ratio. Existing source-specific ECF is unchanged. Solve a calculation in a dehydration/mass-measurement context and communicate the hydration ratio. The supplied masses are data, not a newly measured experiment.
Recall/recognise an approximate atmospheric percentage. No percentage calculation is asked, so ratio/percentage computation is not separately linked.
Complete an electron-pair chemical diagram. Other-science-only geometry rows remain excluded for Chemistry.
Write and balance the named chemical equation. Chemical conservation reasoning is not automatically tagged as an independently assessed algebraic system.
Recall an environmental consequence. No experiment/data-evaluation or mathematical operation is asked.
Select a chemical formula. No independent measurement, experiment-design or numerical demand is established.
Describe two ion-identification procedures and corresponding observations. The task asks known tests rather than an open investigation design with variables/repeats.
Define molecular isomerism. No separate listed experimental or mathematical demand.
Draw chemical connectivity with displayed bonds. Geometry/3D-visualisation rows without Chemistry ticks are not imported to classify this chemistry skill.
Classify a named reaction type; no separate practical or mathematical operation is demanded.
Draw a polymer repeat unit using chemical bonding knowledge; this does not establish a Chemistry-applicable geometry demand.
State consequences of disposal methods. This evaluates an environmental issue, not experimental-data accuracy or validity.
Convert product masses to mole ratios, then solve the oxygen-balance relation. No generic balancing skill is inferred for all symbolic equations.
Complete coefficients and state symbols of the chemical equation. Do not automatically allocate algebra skills solely because chemical coefficients are unknown.
Explain a health effect of a chemical product. No practical inference, data analysis or numeric operation is requested.
Apply reaction knowledge to explain the measured mass change in the given apparatus.
Explain the function of a component in the experimental method.

Interpret numerical/qualitative graph information in the rate explanation. A qualitative changing gradient does not require drawing a tangent, so 4E is not assigned. Apply reaction knowledge to interpret the experimental curve and explain changes in rate and completion. No required tangent construction is inferred.

Translate half the acid amount into half the plateau mass on the graph. Prediction is not automatically tagged as plotting supplied paired data under 4C. Predict and draw a changed experimental curve using the concentration condition and communicate the predicted pattern graphically. This does not supply official AO marks.
Explain the predicted effect of changing chip size using reaction-rate knowledge. Naming a changed condition is not itself a demand to list independent/dependent/control variables.
Complete the products in the source equation. No separate practical or mathematical demand; the historical/current nitric-acid scope qualification remains unresolved.

Read the thermometer and subtract the stated rise to the requested nearest 0.1 degree. This is decimal precision, not a significant-figure rule. Read the thermometer with the specified precision and use the supplied rise to infer the missing temperature. Not an accuracy estimate or an invented repeat measurement.

Use mass, heat capacity and temperature rise in the heat equation; preserve the source rejection of one significant figure. Solve the practical heat-transfer calculation using supplied measurements and communicate its result.

Convert mass to amount, divide heat by amount, convert J to kJ and give the signed result to two significant figures. Use the linked practical heat result to calculate a molar energy change, retaining specified units/sign/precision.
Apply thermal-transfer knowledge to evaluate how a changed container affects measurement accuracy. Accuracy is not silently relabelled repeatability or reliability.

assessmentObjectiveContext.denominator: Whole qualification; Paper 1 table values are percentages of the qualification, not percentages of individual tasks.

blockers: Historical applicability/amendment reconciliation remains pending: the saved September2024 issue postdates the May2024 paper.
All-leaf listed-skill demand is now agent-reviewed, but official per-leaf AO/skill mark allocation has not been obtained and is not inferred from specification weightings.
Measurement/drawing presentation, source-credit calibration and validated templates remain incomplete.
This audit does not establish complete teaching, processing of other papers or human certification.
decisionPolicy: Conservative explicit-demand links. Do not label generic counting as decimal notation, recall of a percentage as percentage computation, bond drawings as geometry, balancing as automatic algebra, qualitative slope as a tangent construction, known-test description as open investigation planning, accuracy as reliability, or a named changed condition as a variable-identification task. No additive skill marks are derived from overlapping links.
